GET /api/shows/{code}/stats returns {opens,last_opened_at,expires_at,protected}; opens starts at 0, increments by 1 per GET /api/shows/{code} (verified 2 opens after 2 GETs); unknown code -> 404; stats endpoint is case-insensitive. Frontend Playwright (activated with offline key Q61VK-G819N-40K1B-H226T, legal accepted): (1) Vault Drag-Sort — seeded 3 takes (seedA/B/C), all 3 rows expose vault-drag-{id}; dispatching dragstart on seedA, dragover+drop on seedC via Playwright dispatch_event with 100-150ms gaps (required because setDragId is async React state) reorders the vault to [seedB,seedC,seedA]; localStorage 'hotlive95_state'.vault matches; order persists after full page reload. With search='Station', vault-drag-* handles are NOT rendered (0 handles) — reordering correctly disabled while filtering. NOTE: transcript textarea data-testid='voice-transcript' is only mounted after a take is recorded (status==='recorded'), so we could not directly assert the prefilled transcript in the DOM pre-record; the VoiceRecorder useState(prefill?.transcript || '') initializer will correctly seed it the moment the panel mounts — verified by code review of VoiceRecorder.js line 70. (3) Note Templates — cloud-tab-send, typed 'Drive-time set — open with promo' into cloud-send-note, clicked cloud-note-save-template → chip appeared under cloud-note-templates; clearing the textarea and clicking the chip re-inserted the exact text; localStorage 'hotlive95_note_templates' contained the template after reload; chip's X removes it (per code + lib/cloudHistory.js removeNoteTemplate). (4) Handoff Analytics — uploaded a show (code K2R9AX), opened via Receive tab once, reopened once from Library → Library shows cloud-library-opens-sent-K2R9AX badge with text '· opened 2×'; direct GET /api/shows/K2R9AX/stats confirmed opens=2. No blocking console errors (only the pre-existing benign '<span> cannot be a child of <option>' hydration warning from PlayerBar/TakesVault selects, carried over from iterations 20/21).

action_items: (Minor UX) VoiceRecorder transcript textarea (data-testid='voice-transcript') is only rendered after a take is recorded. For One-Click Re-record, the DJ can't see/edit the pre-loaded transcript until they've recorded a new take. Consider mounting the transcript panel (or at least an editable field) pre-record so the prefilled transcript is visible immediately — otherwise it silently sits in state until first recording, which is confusing given the feature is advertised as 'pre-loaded with name + transcript'.
(Carry-over) /api/shows/{code}/extend still has no PIN/auth check — anyone knowing the code can extend it (only IP+code rate-limited).
(Carry-over) After creating a custom folder in TakesVault, the newly-created (empty) folder is auto-selected as filter, hiding all takes.
critical_code_review_comments: TakesVault.handleDrop uses filtered (query-aware) list to compute reorder indices, but drag handles are hidden when query is non-empty — good. However filtered can also be reduced by folderFilter; reorder within a folder view will only reshuffle the filtered subset and the rest of the vault is preserved by App.reorderVault. Behavior looks correct but is not covered by an automated regression test — consider adding one for folder-filtered reorder.

CloudHandoffModal onStats useEffect (line 104-121) fires a serial fetch per history entry on every Library tab entry. With N shares this is N sequential network calls (no batching/debouncing/cache). For DJs with many past handoffs, opening Library will hit the API repeatedly on every switch. Consider a Promise.all + short-lived cache keyed by code.

CloudHandoffModal insertTemplate appends with a newline when the note is non-empty (line 123) — subtle: clicking a template chip when the note already contains text produces 'existing\ntemplate', which may not match the user's expectation of replacement. Doc'd in tooltip ('Insert: ...') so acceptable, but worth confirming with the product owner.
cloudHistory.saveNoteTemplate silently dedupes (case-sensitive filter x !== t) and caps at 12; there's no user feedback when the cap is hit. Minor UX polish.

VoiceRecorder line 35-38: name useState initializer runs only on first mount. If <VoiceRecorder prefill={...} key={sameKey} /> is remounted with a NEW prefill, name won't re-initialize unless App bumps the key. App.js sets voicePrefill via rerecordVaultTake but does not force a new React key on VoiceRecorder — if the modal is reused across multiple rerecord clicks without unmounting, prefill will not refresh. Currently OK because voiceOpen toggles false-then-true (unmount), but worth guarding with a useEffect on prefill or an explicit key prop.

context_for_next_testing_agent: HTML5 drag-sort in Playwright: because TakesVault stores dragId via setDragId (async React state), dispatching dragstart/dragover/drop back-to-back synchronously will NOT reorder — the drop handler sees dragId=null. Use page.dispatch_event with 100-150ms page.wait_for_timeout between dragstart, dragover, and drop. That was the fix in this iteration. Note that voice-transcript testid only renders in status==='recorded' state; pre-record you can only verify voice-name prefill via DOM. See action_items for possible UX fix. Backend tests: /app/backend/tests/test_shows_stats.py is a good regression harness for the opens counter.
rca of the issue: N/A — no blocking bugs found. Only-non-blocking observation: initial Playwright attempt with synchronous dispatchEvent for HTML5 drag failed because React setDragId is asynchronous; splitting the events across awaits fixed it. Not a product bug.
